edges.description: Ligand blockade produces hypervascularization, failure of arteriovenous specification, and multiple large arteriovenous malformations in the neonatal retina.
edges.limitations: Acute antibody-mediated depletion of both BMP9 and BMP10 in a neonate is not a germline GDF2 variant: it removes both ligands rather than one, acts over days rather than a lifetime, and is read out in the retina, which is not a site of human HHT5 disease. It therefore models the consequence of losing circulating ligand, not the natural history of the human disease. Note that the biallelic human cases lose circulating BMP10 as well as BMP9, which is the state this dual blockade most closely resembles.

edges.description: Complete germline loss of bmp9 does not produce arteriovenous malformations in this organism.
edges.limitations: Zebrafish carry duplicate BMP10 paralogs (bmp10 and bmp10-like) that cover for bmp9 loss, so the negative result is a statement about ligand redundancy in this species rather than evidence that BMP9 is dispensable in humans. Human biallelic GDF2 patients lose circulating BMP10 as well as BMP9, a state this single-gene mutant does not model. Note also that this mutant result contradicts the earlier bmp9 morpholino knockdown reported in the founding HHT5 paper - see the hht5_zebrafish_morphant_mutant discussion.

edges.description: Transient bmp9 knockdown produced an angiogenic phenotype, supporting a role for BMP9 in angiogenesis but not reproducing the human vascular lesion.

nodes.description: Interstitial deletions larger than five megabases spanning 10q11.22 to 10q11.23 and including GDF2, in two of four probands in one cohort - the first report of large genomic deletions causing HHT5. Two consequences follow. Diagnostically, sequencing alone cannot find these; CNV-aware testing is required. Phenotypically, a multi-megabase deletion removes many genes besides GDF2, and the extravascular findings in these patients were attributed to the deletion rather than to BMP9 loss - so do not read their non-vascular features as HHT5 phenotypes.

nodes.description: The tissue lesion is a direct artery-to-vein connection without an intervening capillary bed - a telangiectasis where small and superficial, an arteriovenous malformation where large or visceral. In HHT5 the reported distribution is distinctive rather than simply a milder version of HHT: the cutaneous lesions are spider-like or linear and fall on the cheeks, chin and face rather than on the lips, oral cavity and finger pads that the Curacao criteria specify, and the pulmonary lesions tend to be numerous, tiny and diffuse rather than discrete feeding-vessel AVMs. The one reported heterozygous family is the exception on the cutaneous side, with telangiectasia its authors called typical of HHT.

nodes.description: BMP9 is synthesised as a precursor consisting of a prodomain and a C-terminal growth-factor domain, cleaved by furin-type proprotein convertases so that the prodomain remains non-covalently bound to the mature dimer. The two functionally characterised HHT5 missense alleles do not abolish expression of the precursor; they block this maturation step. Cells transfected with the p.Cys428Arg construct expressed the proprotein but secreted no mature BMP9 dimer, and conditioned medium from the mutant failed to induce the BMP target genes ID1 and pre-miR-21 in endothelial cells. The truncating alleles act earlier and more completely: p.Gln26Ter protein could be translated from an internal methionine but was neither processed nor secreted.

nodes.description: BMP9 is secreted principally by the liver and circulates in plasma; BMP10 levels track it closely, partly through circulating BMP9/BMP10 heterodimers. In children homozygous for GDF2 nonsense alleles, plasma BMP9 and BMP10 were both undetectable and serum-derived endothelial BMP activity was correspondingly low. In the heterozygous classic-HHT family, circulating BMP9 was significantly reduced rather than absent. This node is the systemic step that makes HHT5 a ligand-deficiency disease, in contrast to the receptor and co-receptor haploinsufficiencies of HHT2 and HHT1, and it is the reason plasma BMP9 is a candidate biomarker for this entity specifically.

nodes.description: The working model for the whole HHT series is that BMP9/BMP10 signalling through ALK1 and endoglin holds endothelium in a quiescent state, and that losing it re-activates angiogenesis or sensitises the endothelium to angiogenic stimuli, producing endothelial hyperproliferation and hypermigration. Direct demonstration for the GDF2 lesion specifically is animal and in vitro: a bmp9-deficient zebrafish showed BMP9 is required in angiogenesis, and mutant BMP9 conditioned medium failed to induce ID1 in cultured endothelial cells. Marked PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED because the quiescence-to-AVM step is inferred from the shared pathway and from model systems rather than observed in HHT5 patient tissue.

nodes.description: Losing the BMP9/ALK1-SMAD1/5/8 input does not merely remove a brake; it releases two proliferative signalling arms. In HHT models, endothelial PI3K/Akt/mTOR and VEGFR2 signalling become overactivated, and correcting them pharmacologically blocks and reverses arteriovenous malformations. The reason this node belongs in a GDF2 entry rather than only in the parent disease is the model used: the malformations were produced by BMP9/BMP10 immunoblockade, which is a ligand-deficiency model and therefore the closest available experimental analogue of HHT5 itself. It is nonetheless a mouse model and not a GDF2 patient, so the node is marked PROVISIONAL. It is also the mechanistic rationale for the single reported sirolimus response in this entity.

nodes.description: BMP9 and BMP10 bind a heterotetrameric endothelial receptor complex of two ALK1 type-I receptors and two type-II receptors (BMPR-II, ActR-IIA or ActR-IIB), with endoglin as co-receptor, and signal through phosphorylation of SMAD1/5/8 and complex formation with SMAD4. Loss of ligand therefore converges on exactly the pathway that ACVRL1 (ALK1, HHT2), ENG (endoglin, HHT1) and SMAD4 variants disrupt at the receptor, co-receptor and effector levels - which is the mechanistic reason a ligand disease sits inside the HHT series at all.

nodes.description: A ligand-depletion rather than a genotype model: blocking antibodies against BMP9 and BMP10 are injected into lactating dams and reach the pups through milk, depleting circulating ligand during postnatal retinal angiogenesis. This is the closest available experimental analogue of the HHT5 lesion, because HHT5 is itself a circulating-ligand deficiency, and it is the only model in this entry that positively reproduces the human vascular lesion - the two zebrafish entries are a negative result and a transient knockdown.

The transient knockdown used in the founding HHT5 report, which the authors read as showing BMP9 involvement in angiogenesis. It is recorded here beside the germline mutant because the two disagree, and because a curator reading only the founding paper would take this as settled.

Germline zebrafish bmp9 mutants survive to adulthood with no overt phenotype, while combined loss of the duplicate BMP10 paralogs is embryonic-lethal with cranial arteriovenous malformations indistinguishable from acvrl1 mutants. The model is informative for HHT5 precisely because it fails: it says that removing BMP9 alone, in an animal that retains BMP10, is tolerated, which is the most concrete available explanation for why heterozygous GDF2 carriers are so often unaffected and why biallelic carriers - who lose circulating BMP10 as well - are the ones who present in childhood.
